title: Looking Ahead: Future Continuous and Future Perfect
summary: In this lesson, you will learn how to use two useful future tenses. You will be able to talk about actions in progress and finished actions in the future.

sections.p: Use the future continuous to talk about an action that will be in progress at a specific time in the future. We make it with 'will be' plus the verb ending in '-ing'. Imagine a photo taken at 8 PM tomorrow: what are you doing in that picture? That is when you use this tense.

ex.en: At 8 PM tonight, I will be watching my favorite TV show.
ex.mean: The action starts before 8 PM and continues after 8 PM.

ex.en: Don't call me at noon because I will be having a team meeting.
ex.mean: I am in the middle of a meeting at that exact time.

sections.p: Use the future perfect to talk about an action that will be finished before a specific time in the future. We make it with 'will have' plus the past participle of the verb. Think of it as looking back from a point in the future to say something is already done.

ex.en: By next Friday, I will have finished my big project.
ex.mean: The project is complete before next Friday arrives.

ex.en: She will have moved to a new apartment by the end of June.
ex.mean: The moving process is done prior to July.

sections.p: Sometimes people confuse these two tenses, but they have different meanings. The future continuous focuses on the journey or process happening at a future time. The future perfect focuses on the final result achieved by a future deadline. Choose the right one depending on whether you care about the process or the finish line.

ex.en: At 10 AM, I will be working on the report.
ex.mean: I am in the middle of writing it right then.

ex.en: By 10 AM, I will have sent the report.
ex.mean: The task is completely done before 10 AM.

tip: Remember 'will be' for actions happening across time, and 'will have' for deadlines where things are already finished.

quiz.en: This time tomorrow, we ___ on a sunny beach.
By next year, they ___ a new house.
Don't visit at 3 PM because I ___ for my exam.
She ___ cooking dinner by the time you arrive.
By the end of the month, I ___ all my books.
